blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Small talk sounds simple, but doing it well is a skill. Good small-talkers do two things differently. First, they open rather than close: "What did you get up to at the weekend?" beats "Had a good weekend?" because it invites a real story instead of a quick yes or no.

Second, they listen for small hooks and gently follow them. Someone mentions a walk in the Lake District? Ask where. Someone mentions a new coffee place? Ask if it's any good. This turns two minutes of polite noise into the beginning of an actual relationship.

The British are very loyal to the small-talkers who remember the details from last week. "How was the wedding, by the way?" at the start of a call is often worth a quarter of an hour of hard selling.

items.q: According to the text, why does "What did you get up to at the weekend?" work better than "Had a good weekend?"
options: It invites a real story instead of a yes or no
It avoids talking about the weekend
items.why: "it invites a real story instead of a quick yes or no" — a pergunta aberta abre espaço para uma resposta longa.

items.q: What is the second thing that good small-talkers do differently?
options: They listen for hooks and gently follow them
items.why: "they listen for small hooks and gently follow them".

items.q: What does the writer suggest by comparing small talk to "a quarter of an hour of hard selling"?
options: Small talk should replace every sales meeting
Remembering a personal detail can build more trust than aggressive selling
Clients dislike any form of selling
Hard selling is always the fastest route to a deal
items.why: Inferência: lembrar do casamento vale mais que 15 minutos de venda dura — o vínculo pesa mais que a pressão.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Small talk is an empty ritual with no business value
Following a hook can turn small talk into a relationship
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro defende que o small talk bem feito tem valor real de negócio.

items.q: The phrase "polite noise" suggests that, without a hook, small talk is…
options: the most important part of a meeting
pleasant but empty until someone builds on it
items.why: Inferência: "ruído educado" é agradável mas vazio — só vira relação quando alguém segue um gancho.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily orientando uma nova colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, so you've got a call with the São Paulo client in ten minutes, and I can see you're already rehearsing the numbers. Good — but do me a favour and don't open with the numbers.

Open with a question. And make it a proper one. Not "Did you have a nice weekend?" — she'll just say "yes, fine" and you've got nowhere to go. Try "What did you get up to?" or "How did you find the trip back?" Something she can actually tell a story about.

Then listen. Last week she mentioned her daughter was starting school. If she brings it up again, ask how the first day went. If she doesn't, you bring it up: "How did the first day of school go, by the way?" Trust me, that little detail is worth more than any pitch.

One warning, though. Match her energy. If she's brisk and busy today, keep it to twenty seconds and get to business. Reading the room is the whole game. Overdo the enthusiasm and it sounds fake.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily tell her colleague NOT to do at the start of the call?
items.why: "don't open with the numbers."

items.q: Why does Emily dislike "Did you have a nice weekend?"
options: The client will just say "yes, fine" and leave nowhere to go
It takes too long to answer
items.why: "she'll just say 'yes, fine' and you've got nowhere to go" — é uma pergunta fechada.

items.q: What does Emily say about the daughter starting school?
options: It is a detail worth more than any pitch
It is a private topic to avoid
It should only be raised if the client raises it first
It is not relevant to the call
items.why: "that little detail is worth more than any pitch" — e Emily sugere trazer o assunto de volta você mesma.

items.q: What does Emily most likely mean by "reading the room is the whole game"?
options: You should always talk for the same length of time
Adjusting your approach to the other person's mood matters most
You should let the client lead every topic
Meetings should be held in a quiet room
items.why: Inferência: se a cliente está apressada, corte o small talk — ajustar-se ao clima é o essencial.

items.q: What can we infer about Emily's overall advice?
options: She believes enthusiasm should always be maximised
She values genuine, well-judged connection over a scripted pitch
She wants the colleague to avoid business topics
She thinks small talk is a waste of time
items.why: Inferência: ela prioriza a conexão real e bem calibrada, e avisa contra o entusiasmo forçado.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She mentioned her trip to Portugal, so I used it as a hook to keep the chat going." A hook is…
options: a detail you can follow to continue the conversation
a way to end a call politely
items.why: Hook = gancho: um detalhe que você segue para manter a conversa viva.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "'Did you enjoy the conference?' is a ___ — it usually gets a yes or a no."
items.why: Closed question = pergunta fechada: rende só sim ou não.

items.q: "He always remembers a small detail from the last meeting." A detail is…
options: a small, specific piece of information
items.why: Detail = detalhe: um pequeno dado específico, como o casamento ou a viagem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Clients stay ___ to people who take a genuine interest in them."
items.why: Loyal = fiel: o cliente permanece leal a quem se interessa de verdade por ele.

items.q: "For the first minute it was just polite noise, then she found a real topic." Polite noise means…
items.why: Polite noise = ruído educado: conversa agradável mas ainda sem conteúdo real.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de relacionamento com clientes. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "A good open question helps the other person open up." To open up means to…
options: start speaking more freely and share more
items.why: Open up = abrir-se: falar mais à vontade e compartilhar mais.

items.q: "She promised to follow up on his question about the shipment." To follow up means to…
options: take further action or check back on it later
items.why: Follow up = dar continuidade, retomar o assunto depois.

items.q: "I'll touch base with the client before the review." To touch base means to…
options: make brief contact to stay in sync
items.why: Touch base = dar um alô rápido para se alinhar.

items.q: "Let's not rush the numbers — let's break the ice first." To break the ice means to…
options: make people feel relaxed at the start
items.why: Break the ice = quebrar o gelo: deixar as pessoas à vontade no começo.

items.q: "Remembering that detail really helped the relationship take off." To take off means to…
items.why: Take off = deslanchar: começar a crescer e dar certo.
